Edge-case analysis: (1) ViewLocator.Build(null) returns null — handled. (2) ViewModel type whose view is not in the assembly → TextBlock fallback — handled. (3) App.Services null when view type resolved → NullReferenceException — acceptable programming-error contract, not a regression.

comments.note: ViewLocator.Build(): if a ViewModel's derived view type IS resolved from the assembly but is not registered in App.Services, GetRequiredService(viewType) throws InvalidOperationException with no fallback. Tests cover all 5 registered views only. A future ViewModel pointing to an unregistered view would surface as a runtime exception at the point of navigation, not at startup.

No test covers the ViewLocator.Build(null) → null return path, nor the 'view type not found in assembly' → TextBlock fallback. Both are trivially correct per inspection of ViewLocator.cs but are not exercised by the test suite.

BuildShellViewModel() passes _ => null as the IDatabaseConnector factory parameter. Tests pass because no test triggers the factory, but any future test that exercises the connect flow through ShellViewModel would receive a null connector and could produce confusing failures.
